item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ultrapassou o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e liderava a apuração do segundo turno da eleição presidencial deste domingo com 50,08% dos votos válidos, enquanto o presidente Lula somava 49,92%, com 15,06% das seções eleitorais apuradas, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

item.title: Real Madrid derrota 2-1 al Barcelona en el Camp Nou con doblete de Mbappé y se acerca
item.description: El Real Madrid se convirtió el domingo en el primer equipo en vencer al Barcelona en LaLiga esta temporada al vencer 2-1 al campeón defensor en el Camp Nou con un doblete de Kylian Mbappé.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: El Real Madrid se convirtió el domingo en el primer equipo en vencer al Barcelona en LaLiga esta temporada al vencer 2-1 al campeón defensor en el Camp Nou con un doblete de Kylian Mbappé. El undécimo gol de Mbappé en 10 partidos de LaLiga le dio la victoria al DT José Mourinho en su regreso al Clásico 13 años después de que terminara su primera etapa en el Real Madrid. Con el triunfo, los blancos redujeron la diferencia con el Barcelona a solo tres puntos. En una primera parte muy igualada, ambos equipos crearon una serie de ocasiones de gol, pero las incursiones ofensivas del Madrid tuvieron mucha más determinación. La frustración de Hansi Flick en la banda sirvió como prueba de que el plan de juego de Mourinho estaba funcionando mejor que el suyo. En el minuto 41, Yan Diomande centró desde la izquierda y el despeje suave de Gerard Martin rebotó en Mbappé, que salía a su encuentro, y el balón acabó en el fondo de la red. El Barcelona tuvo la oportunidad de empatar antes del descanso tras un rebote, pero Lamine Yamal no pudo convertir desde cerca. El Barca igualó en el minuto 61, cuando un pase de Pedri encontró a Raphinha con espacio en el área. El brasileño remató cruzado para poner el 1-1. La rápida circulación del balón del Madrid en su propio campo siguió dejando al descubierto la defensa del Barcelona en los primeros compases de la segunda parte, pero tras el gol, a los visitantes les resultó cada vez más difícil escapar de la presión del conjunto culé. Pese a todo, la defensa del Madrid logró sostenerse, y el equipo de Mourinho seguía generando peligro en ataque. Esa convicción defensiva tuvo su recompensa a tres minutos del final. Un mal control de Gabriel Jesus propició un contraataque del Madrid. Eduardo Camavinga logró colarse entre la defensa antes de pasarle el balón a Mbappé, quien solo tuvo que empujarlo a la red vacía. El triunfo fue lo suficientemente convincente como para sugerir que el Madrid supondrá un serio desafío al título para el equipo catalán tras dos temporadas decepcionantes. "Ha sido un gran partido, que seguramente todo el mundo que ama el fútbol se ha parado para ver, con dos equipos que jugaron a ganar y en nuestro caso (...) los chicos han hecho un partido extraordinario, muy organizados, concentrados, con coraje para salir jugando desde atrás con un adversario que presiona mucho", dijo Mourinho tras el encuentro. El Barcelona se mantiene líder de LaLiga con 27 puntos en 10 partidos, uno más que el Atlético de Madrid, que aparece segundo. El Real Madrid, tercero, suma 24 unidades.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude accessed public US state of Georgia voter information, Axios reports
item.description: Anthropic's Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia voter data without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic's Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia voter data without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday. "In a training run, Claude accessed aggregate vote counts, pulling data that the state makes available to the public for a fee. It didn't access the state's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records," an Anthropic spokesperson told Axios. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: Real Madrid vence Barcelona no Camp Nou
item.description: O Real Madrid tornou-se neste domingo a primeira equipe a derrotar o Barcelona na atual temporada da LaLiga, ao vencer o clássico por 2 a 1 no Camp Nou, com dois gols de Kylian Mbappé.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: O Real Madrid tornou-se neste domingo a primeira equipe a derrotar o Barcelona na atual temporada da LaLiga, ao vencer o clássico por 2 a 1 no Camp Nou, com dois gols de Kylian Mbappé. O atacante francês abriu o placar aos 41 minutos do primeiro tempo ao desviar para o gol uma tentativa de corte de Gerard Martín. O Barcelona empatou aos 16 minutos da etapa final. Após uma cobrança rápida de escanteio, Pedri encontrou Raphinha livre na área, e o brasileiro bateu no canto, sem chances para o goleiro Andriy Lunin. Quando a partida parecia caminhar para o empate, Eduardo Camavinga avançou pela esquerda e cruzou para Mbappé marcar o gol da vitória aos 42 minutos do segundo tempo. Apesar da derrota, o Barcelona segue na liderança da LaLiga, com 27 pontos em 10 jogos, um a mais que o vice-líder Atlético de Madrid. O Real Madrid ocupa a terceira colocação, com 24 pontos. (Reportagem de Ruairidh Barlow)

item.title: UK commits to further £432 million to end rough sleeping
item.description: Britain's government said on Sunday it would almost double its funding for efforts to end rough sleeping and give homeless people a way to get off the streets in the winter months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's government said on Sunday it would almost double its funding for efforts to end rough sleeping and give homeless people a way to get off the streets in the winter months. Prime Minister Andy Burnham and finance minister John Healey said they would commit a further £432 million ($577.7 million) of funding for the plan, which offers accommodation and support, to run until the scheduled end of parliament in 2029. Burnham said on his first day in Downing Street in July that he wanted to end rough sleeping. He was due to meeting local leaders, businesses and charities on Monday to discuss the plan. Healey is scheduled to announce his first budget plan on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: Leafs riding 'great' vibes while Flames try to finish perfect homestand
item.description: The Calgary Flames and visiting Toronto Maple Leafs will strive to continue their win streaks in the face of key injury absences when they meet on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Calgary Flames and visiting Toronto Maple Leafs will strive to continue their win streaks in the face of key injury absences when they meet on Monday night. The Maple Leafs will wrap up the Alberta section of their road trip coming off the high point of their season so far. Toronto scored four third-period goals in a 7-2 battering of Edmonton on Saturday to extend its winning streak to four games, its first of that length since January. "The vibes are great," said goaltender Anthony Stolarz, who made 30 saves on the night. "We got a great group, an influx of kids that have a lot of energy, and they're really bringing out the best in everyone. It's an exciting time to be a Maple Leaf." The ongoing absence of second-line center John Tavares (lower-body injury) has afforded head coach Jim Hiller the opportunity to prove that the Maple Leafs' forward corps offers more than the one-two punch of years past. Thirteen different players recorded a point on Saturday, and every member of the fourth line -- Brandon Duhaime, Teddy Blueger and Zack MacEwen -- nabbed their first goal in blue and white over the last two games. As a team, Toronto has scored 18 goals over the last three. "That to me says something about your team. That says you've got depth. That says it's not just (Auston) Matthews. It's not just (William) Nylander. It's not just Tavares. It's going through the lineup, and that gives you a chance to win every night," Hiller said. Toronto conceded its first power-play goal on the road against the Oilers, though they still lead the NHL in penalty kill percentage (95.2%) and special-teams efficiency (125.4%). After losing six of their first seven games, the Flames will have a chance to extend their own winning streak to four as they wrap up their four-game homestand. Devin Cooley made 28 saves as Calgary thumped the Detroit Red Wings 4-1 Saturday. "We've just been stacking wins and stacking good play the last couple games here," said Joel Farabee, who had three points on the night. "We just have a little bit of confidence and a little bit of swagger right now that maybe we didn't have the first five or six games of the season. We're just finding how we have to play to win and just trying not to do too much and playing simple." The Flames have managed to reverse their fortunes with something of a depleted offense. Jonathan Huberdeau (hip) remains sidelined for the foreseeable future while captain Mikael Backlund (upper-body injury) has missed the last two outings. Lacking genuine star power at the top of their lineup, Calgary will continue to count on a distributed workload and a high-functioning power play, which is 6-for-12 over its last four games. Nine of the team's 12 forwards logged at least twelve minutes at even strength against Detroit. "When the power play is scoring and things are going their way, they start feeling really good about playing on the ice and they know they can be difference-makers and that's the phase they're in right now," said head coach Ryan Huska. Toronto will likely continue to rotate players in and out of their defensive pairings amid the injury absences of Chris Tanev, Nick Blankenburg and Marshall Rifai. The Maple Leafs have won the last eight encounters between the two teams. --Field Level Media

item.title: New-look Heat search for first win as Mavericks visit
item.description: With three losses to open the season, the Miami Heat are still looking for the first win of the Giannis Antetokounmpo Era.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: With three losses to open the season, the Miami Heat are still looking for the first win of the Giannis Antetokounmpo Era. The Heat get another shot at that elusive victory on Monday night when they play host to the Dallas Mavericks. Antetokounmpo averaged 35.5 points in his first two games in a Heat uniform, but he was held to 14 on Saturday in a 115-110 loss at Charlotte. He played just 25 minutes before fouling out with 1:57 remaining. A 10-time All-Star, two-time NBA MVP and one-time league champion, Antetokounmpo was the prize in the huge offseason trade with the Milwaukee Bucks. But the question then -- and now -- was whether Miami gave up too much to get him. Specifically, do the Heat have enough shooters to put around him? Bam Adebayo, Miami's other established star, is off to a slow start as he averages 13.0 points and 7.0 rebounds per game. Point guard Davion Mitchell has stepped up, averaging 17.0 points on 46.7% 3-point shooting. Both numbers would easily be career highs for Mitchell, a player known more for tight defense. Aside from those three players, nobody on the Heat averages more than 10.3 points. Andrew Wiggins (18.2% on 3-point attempts) and Tim Hardaway Jr. (17.6% from deep) are off to poor shooting starts that are similar to Adebayo (23.1%) and Antetokounmpo (16.7%). Miami coach Erik Spoelstra knows it's early, though, and said this is all part of this version of the Heat learning to handle adversity. "We're all on the same page when shots are going down," Spoelstra said after the loss to Charlotte. "But when the game goes the other way, we really introduce ourselves to each other and collectively build a resolve." Meanwhile, the Mavericks are coming off a 122-106 home loss to San Antonio on Saturday. Dallas played without reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, who injured his left shoulder in a 121-105 win over Indiana on Friday and will be re-evaluated this week. Nine-time All-Star Kyrie Irving, coming off knee surgery, also sat against San Antonio but is expected to be ready to face the Heat. Without that duo on Saturday, Dallas was led by rookie reserve Sergio de Larrea, the No. 25 pick in this year's draft (by the Los Angeles Lakers). A native of Spain, de Larrea is a skilled combo guard listed at 6-foot-5 and 175 pounds. At age 20, he offers Dallas hope that he could develop into a star. He produced 21 points, five rebounds and four assists in 33 minutes against the Spurs after going scoreless in eight minutes during the Mavs' first two games. "Today it was me, but other days it will be other guys," said de Larrea. "I'm waiting every day for this moment. I'm just trying to be prepared, but I have a lot to improve." Irving, if he's ready, will try to improve on his 19.5 scoring average. Flagg leads the team with 23.0 points per game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australia's NEXTDC CEO to forgo fiscal 2027 bonuses after forecast cut, project delay
item.description: NEXTDC CEO Craig Scroggie will give up his fiscal 2027 bonus opportunities, the Australian data centre operator said on Monday, after it slashed its revenue forecast and paused future developments last week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: NEXTDC (NXT.AX) CEO Craig Scroggie will give up his fiscal 2027 bonus opportunities, the Australian data centre operator said on Monday, after it slashed its revenue forecast and paused future developments [USN:L4N4661TS TEXT:"last week"]. Here are some details: The company said the board has withdrawn the resolution proposing an approval of grant of performance rights and restricted rights to the CEO under the fiscal 2027 long term incentive plan. Current Chairman Douglas Flynn has reaffirmed his intention to retire from the board once a new chairman is in place, after a short handover period. The board expects to appoint two new non-executive directors in the first calendar quarter of 2027, NEXTDC added. The company said the board has also withdrawn the resolution seeking shareholder approval to increase the maximum aggregate annual remuneration of non-executive directors by A$300,000 ($210,660), with the incumbent non-executive directors also agreeing to an immediate voluntary 10% reduction in their current fees. Last week, NEXTDC said delays to electricity network upgrades at one of its major Melbourne projects would mean about A$140 million worth of contracted customer revenue this financial year would be deferred. The firm is set to hold its annual general meeting on November 20. ($1 = 1.4241 Australian dollars)

item.title: Wizards, Hornets out to capitalize on early-season momentum
item.description: The Washington Wizards and host Charlotte Hornets have plenty of positives to build on heading into their meeting Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Washington Wizards and host Charlotte Hornets have plenty of positives to build on heading into their meeting Monday night. Both teams won Saturday, providing encouraging signs early in the season. Still, nothing has come easily for the Hornets in their first two home games. They lost by 47 points to Atlanta before watching a 23-point lead evaporate against Miami, then recovering to win 115-110. Brandon Miller led the way with 34 points against the Heat, matching the third-highest total of his four-year career. "Every game is not going to be perfect," Miller said. "Our mindset, other teams are going to go on runs and it's how we respond to it." The Wizards won their road opener 124-120 at Chicago on Saturday, with Trae Young scoring 25 points. Young will be a familiar opponent for Charlotte after making numerous appearances against the Hornets with the Atlanta Hawks. He has led Washington in scoring in each of the past two games after Anthony Davis poured in 34 points in the opener. "We were able to establish physicality," Wizards coach Brian Keefe said. "We stayed with it, and that was the part that was really great." Washington also likes what it has seen from Kyshawn George, particularly his ability to defend bigger players, according to Keefe. "That's why this team is so fun to coach because they want to put the time in," Keefe said. "Kyshawn is right at the top." No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa has yet to make his Wizards debut while dealing with a left ankle injury. He will miss his fourth consecutive game Monday. Washington has shown depth, however, with 10 players seeing action against Chicago. In Saturday's victory, the Hornets benefited from late-game contributions by veteran newcomers Naz Reid and Grayson Allen. It was Charlotte's first home win of the season. "I think they're a big piece of what we're building here," Miller said. "Those are guys who have obviously been to the playoffs and been to places we want to be." Reid said he recognized how quickly the home crowd had embraced his play. Charlotte's veteran core will look to make an impact in close games as the season progresses. "We've been in enough of those situations in our past," Reid said. "Knowing how to keep our composure. ... Those are fun, especially with the home crowd." Hornets coach Charles Lee said the early-season games provide valuable opportunities to evaluate the team, adding that veteran Dennis Schroder has shown he can be a defensive presence. "Just really impressed with the whole group," Lee said. Miller has shot 29.7% from the field through three games after shooting nearly 43% for his career. "That's why you never overreact to shooting numbers or shooting slumps," Lee said. "That guy has a body of work that is just very impressive." The Hornets played their first three games without Kon Knueppel (hamstring), Coby White (calf) and Grant Williams (hamstring). Knueppel resumed individual on-court activity nearly a week ago, but no target date has been set for his return. Charlotte swept the four-game season series in 2025-26 after Washington won the previous five matchups. --Field Level Media

item.title: Real Madrid defeat Barcelona at Camp Nou to halve gap to LaLiga leaders
item.description: Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe. Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended. Real halved the gap to league leaders Barcelona to three points. Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager Hansi Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's game plan was functioning better than his own. In the 41st minute, Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range. It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner. Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing. Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward. That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, before squaring the ball for Mbappe to tap into the empty net. Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place. Third-place Real Madrid are on 24 points. Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe 4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

item.title: Lars Eller scores first goal as Panther in narrow win over Blackhawks
item.description: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday. Panthers goaltender Akira Schmid stopped 20 shots as Florida snapped a two-game losing streak. Schmid turned aside Cole Smith on a breakaway with 5:45 to keep the game tied at 2. Eller netted his first goal of the season at 17:37 of the third period as the Panthers caught the Blackhawks in a line change. Eller took a long pass from Aaron Ekblad just inside the blue line, weaved down the right side and ripped a wrist shot from the circle past Chicago goaltender Spencer Knight. For the 37-old-year Eller, it was also his first goal as a member of the Florida Panthers. He started his NHL career with the St. Louis Blues in the 2009-10 season and has played for the Montreal Canadiens (2010-16), Washington Capitals (2016-23, 2024-25), Colorado Avalanche (2023), Pittsburgh Penguins (2023-25) and Ottawa Senators (2025-26). Special-teams struggles hurt the Blackhawks, who went 0-for-7 on the power play while also failing to capitalize on other chances at even strength. Knight made 29 saves. Chicago managed just six shots in the first period, but one of the club's early attempts provided a 1-0 lead. Ryan Greene tracked a puck that bounced at the top of the crease and into the air and batted it past Schmid and into the net. Andrew Mangiapane earned the primary assist in his return to the lineup; the forward had been out after suffering a lower-body injury in the club's season opener on Sept. 29. Florida tied the game just over four minutes later, as Vilmanis backhanded a loose puck past Knight after the backstop made a save on Sam Reinhart. The Panthers took a 2-1 lead on Matthew Tkachuk's power-play goal at 14:21. Tkachuk deflected Seth Jones' shot from the point just five seconds into the man advantage. Chicago netted the equalizer at 11:15 of the second period when Roman Kantserov took a Patrick Kane feed from behind the net and scored on a wrist shot from the right circle. Florida limited Chicago to one shot on goal during a four-minute power-play early in the second period after Carter Verhaeghe was whistled for a high-sticking double-minor against the Blackhawks' Wyatt Kaiser. Verhaeghe sent a wrist shot off the crossbar on a breakaway moments after springing from the penalty box. The Blackhawks fell to 2-4-0 on a seven-game homestand that is set to conclude with Tuesday's visit from the Los Angeles Kings. --Field Level Media

item.title: North Korea tells UN South fabricated landmine incident, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea said it had written to the UN Security Council, accusing South Korea of fabricating a September landmine incident and endangering troops working to fortify the border, state media KCNA reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said it had written to the UN Security Council, accusing South Korea of fabricating a September landmine incident and endangering troops working to fortify the border, state media KCNA reported on Monday. On Sunday, North Korea's UN representative said in a letter Seoul was using the landmine incident to depict Pyongyang's border construction as a military incursion, and warned violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defence, according to KCNA. It concerns explosions on September 21 in the Demilitarised Zone between the two Koreas that seriously hurt two South Korean soldiers. Seoul subsequently said mines North Korea planted south of the Military Demarcation Line that runs through the DMZ caused the blasts. The UN Command said a North Korean mine across the line violated the armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility. North Korea's letter also accused South Korea of opening fire on North Korean personnel, calling it a violation of the UN Charter, which bars the threat or use of force against another state's territorial integrity. Seoul has said it gives warning broadcasts and fires warning shots to make North Korean soldiers return north when they cross the MDL. North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and fences and laying mines near the MDL in recent years. Last Friday, South Korea's defence ministry again [USN:L1N46905T TEXT:"proposed"] military talks with North Korea to reduce the risk of accidental clashes.

item.title: Bulls searching for shooting aim entering clash vs. Celtics
item.description: The Chicago Bulls are still looking for ways to improve their 3-point shooting, an issue that has carried over from the offseason into the early stages of the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Bulls are still looking for ways to improve their 3-point shooting, an issue that has carried over from the offseason into the early stages of the season. Entering Monday night's road game against the Boston Celtics, the Bulls ranked 17th among the 30 NBA teams in 3-point percentage during the 2025-26 regular season but sit last in the league through three games this season at 22.6%. Chicago is averaging 9.3 made 3-pointers on 41.3 attempts per game. "I want them to shoot the ball," Chicago coach Tiago Splitter said following Saturday's 124-120 loss to Washington. "They can shoot. Part of their development is you are open, you got to shoot it. You practice every day; you have to take them in the game. Sometimes it's the shot the other team is giving to you. It's a team thing, not just one player. Everybody's got to be better. We don't have a 7-3 guy that's going to clean up the whole thing. So it's got to be a team effort and awareness." The Bulls went 12-for-43 from 3-point range against the Wizards. Caleb Wilson, the fourth pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, scored a game-high 30 points but went 1-for-9 from beyond the arc. Jalen Smith and Matas Buzelis each went 2-for-7. "We all knew coming into season (3-point shooting was) one of things we've got to get better and develop," Splitter said. "Caleb one of nine, Matas two of seven - those are the guys who are going to take shots. They are going to get better. But shoot (28) percent, you've really got to win the possession game to win when you are not shooting the ball well." Chicago has struggled defensively as well, allowing 128.0 points per game. Only Milwaukee (129.0) has allowed more. Boston bounced back from a season-opening 121-113 loss at Detroit by beating New York 107-103 at home Friday night. item.title: NFL roundup: Falcons harass 49ers into first loss of 2026
item.description: Michael Penix Jr. threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta Falcons' defense forced four turnovers as they claimed a 29-20 victory on Sunday afternoon to hand the visiting San Francisco 49ers their first loss.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Penix Jr. threw for three touchdowns and the Atlanta Falcons' defense forced four turnovers as they claimed a 29-20 victory on Sunday afternoon to hand the visiting San Francisco 49ers their first loss. Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards while rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels picked off a pass and recovered a fumble in the fourth quarter for the Falcons (3-4), who won their first home game of the season. Nick Folk added three field goals. Brock Purdy hit 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions for the 49ers (6-1). Christian McCaffrey rushed for 39 yards and one touchdown while catching six passes for 61 yards. The 49ers built a 14-3 lead on Kaelon Black's 30-yard touchdown run on the first play of the second quarter, but the Falcons responded with 23 unanswered points as Penix completed touchdown strikes to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts Sr. and Drake London. Giants 27, Titans 21 (OT) Devin Singletary ran for a 30-yard touchdown to defeat his former team and propel New York to the walkoff victory over host Houston. J.J. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards to win his debut start for the Giants (4-2-1) and his fifth consecutive start overall. Cam Skattebo had 17 carries for 124 yards, including a 42-yard run the play before Singletary's game-winner, and Malik Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards. C.J. Stroud completed 17 of 28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (2-5), who dropped to 0-4 at home. Woody Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and tight end Dalton Schultz had five catches for 45 yards. Stroud's 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds left forced overtime. Steelers 16, Saints 10 Aaron Rodgers broke a tie with Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown passes list, Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Pittsburgh defeated New Orleans in the first NFL game played in Paris. The Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game after shutting out the Saints (2-5) in the second half in Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of Paris. Rodgers broke a tie with Manning for third place on the all-time list when he completed his 540th career touchdown pass to Darnell Washington in the second quarter. Tyler Shough passed for 278 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Saints, who rushed for just 18 yards -- 130 fewer than Pittsburgh. Browns 27, Titans 24 Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of a victory over Tennessee in Nashville. After Tennessee tied it 24-24 with 58 seconds remaining on Tony Pollard's third touchdown of the day, Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards with 28 seconds left. Szmyt, who missed from 43 yards in the fourth quarter, booted the winner to keep the Browns (5-2) atop the AFC North. Watson eclipsed 300 yards for the first time with the Browns as he completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and an interception. He also rushed for a score. For the Titans (1-6), Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards. Dolphins 28, Jets 25 Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help Miami pick up its first win, beating New York in East Rutherford, N.J. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards without an interception and rushed for 37 yards on eight attempts to help give head coach Jeff Hafley his first NFL victory. Ollie Gordon II ran for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries as the Dolphins (1-5) rushed for 156 yards overall. The Jets (2-5) lost for the fifth time in six games and lost their eighth consecutive game against an AFC East opponent. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Smith's third touchdown pass was a 12-yarder to Mason Taylor, who caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns. Buccaneers 43, Panthers 13 Bucky Irving rushed for 106 yards and two touchdowns, Calijah Kancey returned a fumble 32 yards for a touchdown and Tampa Bay blasted mistake-prone Carolina in Charlotte. Baker Mayfield was back at quarterback for the Buccaneers (2-5) after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb and had an easy return while completing 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards and one touchdown. The Panthers (3-3) committed four turnovers and missed an extra-point kick. Bryce Young was 14-of-27 passing for 163 yards with two interceptions and a touchdown, while losing a fumble. Vikings 16, Colts 10 Kyler Murray passed for 150 yards and a touchdown, and safety Harrison Smith made an interception in the final minutes to preserve a Minnesota victory over Indianapolis in Minneapolis. T.J. Hockenson had the go-ahead touchdown catch for the Vikings (6-0) early in the fourth quarter. Jordan Mason had a team-high 68 rushing yards, and Justin Jefferson caught four passes for 44 yards on seven targets. Will Reichard made three of four field goal attempts. Jonathan Taylor rushed for 95 yards and a touchdown to lead the Colts (2-5). Daniel Jones completed 13 of 22 yards for 108 yards and an interception. Indianapolis fell despite converting 9-of-16 third- and fourth-down chances. Bengals 35, Ravens 13 Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and Cincinnati scored 35 unanswered points to record a victory over host Baltimore. Burrow completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards while leading five touchdown drives in the half as the Bengals (4-2) overcame a 13-0 halftime deficit. Tee Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase, Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample also caught touchdown passes and Samaje Perine rushed for a score. Lamar Jackson (ankle) missed his third straight game for the Ravens (4-3). Tyler "Snoop" Huntley completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 298 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Zay Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards and one score for Baltimore, which blew a double-digit lead for the second straight week. --Field Level Media

item.title: Panthers OT Taylor Moton suffers fractured fibula in loss to Bucs
item.description: Carolina Panthers veteran right tackle Taylor Moton was carted off the field with a fractured left fibula during Sunday's 43-13 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Carolina Panthers veteran right tackle Taylor Moton was carted off the field with a fractured left fibula during Sunday's 43-13 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Panthers coach Dave Canales acknowledged that Moton would be "out for a while" after the contest. It was just Moton's second game since returning from a serious blood clot issue. He was hurt when teammate Rasheed Walker, the left tackle, fell across the back of his legs in the opening minute of the third quarter. Moton held his left leg and punched the turf while waiting for trainers to come on the field. "It was the fibula. There is a fracture there," Canales told reporters. "We'll have to get the full run-up to be able to give you the extent of the whole thing. "But it was just sick for ‘T-Mo.' Working his way back, getting out there. Just kinda an end-of-the-play thing, guys just rolled up on him unexpectedly at that moment." Moton, 32, was diagnosed with blood clots in June and was placed on blood thinners. He began the season on the reserve/non-football injury list and was activated ahead of last week's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. "I feel for T-Mo so much, such a great human being, such a great guy," quarterback Bryce Young said. "He's as resilient as they come. He's going to do everything he can; he's going to work, and he'll bounce back from it, but, yeah, just from the human side, I feel for him." Sunday marked the 130th NFL start (in 147 career games) for Moton, a second-round draft choice in 2017 out of Western Michigan. Monroe Freeling, the team's 2026 first-round draft pick who started the first four games in place of Moten, finished the game at right tackle. Freeling played at Georgia. --Field Level Media

item.title: Antonelli gana en EEUU, pero tendrá que esperar a México para proclamarse campeón de F1
item.description: Kimi Antonelli ganó el domingo el Gran Premio de Estados Unidos con Mercedes, lo que le sitúa a un paso de convertirse en el campeón más joven de la historia de la Fórmula 1 el próximo fin de semana en México.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli ganó el domingo el Gran Premio de Estados Unidos con Mercedes, lo que le sitúa a un paso de convertirse en el campeón más joven de la historia de la Fórmula 1 el próximo fin de semana en México. El italiano de 20 años hizo todo lo posible por poner el campeonato fuera del alcance de sus rivales en Texas, pero Lewis Hamilton, de Ferrari, y su compañero de equipo en Mercedes, George Russell, hicieron lo justo para retrasar lo inevitable al quedar cuarto y octavo, respectivamente. Antonelli solo necesita ahora sumar dos puntos, un noveno puesto, en México para asegurarse el título. Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, terminó segundo, a 13,078 segundos, en la carrera del domingo en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin, mientras que Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, quedó tercero, ayudado por un coche de seguridad virtual en los últimos compases que frenó a un Hamilton que le pisaba los talones y que terminó un segundo más tarde. La contundente victoria desde la largada, con una estrategia de una sola parada, fue la novena de Antonelli esta temporada, y ahora aventaja a Russell en 123 puntos y a Hamilton en 124, cuando quedan un máximo de 125 puntos por ganar, cifra que se reducirá a 100 tras la carrera de México. "Era el resultado que necesitábamos y todo el equipo se lo merece muchísimo", dijo Antonelli. "Sé que estamos muy cerca. Intentamos terminar por todo lo alto y esperamos poder sentenciar el título muy pronto". El vigente campeón de McLaren, Lando Norris, terminó quinto, mientras que Isack Hadjar, de Red Bull, fue sexto, por delante de Oscar Piastri, de McLaren. Liam Lawson fue noveno con Racing Bulls y Pierre Gasly se llevó el último punto para Alpine. Antonelli realizó una salida fulgurante y llegó a tener una ventaja de 2,3 segundos al final de la primera vuelta, mientras que los dos pilotos de Ferrari se enzarzaron en una lucha por el segundo puesto con Verstappen, que había tenido una salida lenta. Leclerc se adelantó, antes de que el Red Bull le volviera a pasar, y estuvo a punto de chocar con Hamilton tras un embotellamiento. El coche de seguridad virtual se activó brevemente en la segunda vuelta para permitir a los comisarios retirar los restos del asfalto, y a Russell se le impuso una penalización de cinco segundos por obtener ventaja sobre Piastri en la primera vuelta, en la curva 13. "Yo estaba por el interior, él adelantaba por el exterior, ese es su riesgo", dijo Russell por radio antes de la sanción. Ollie Bearman, de Haas, también recibió una penalización de 10 segundos por provocar una colisión con Gasly y se retiró a mitad de carrera.

item.title: Antonelli wins US Grand Prix but must wait for title
item.description: Kimi Antonelli won the US Grand Prix for Mercedes on Sunday to stand on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion in Mexico next weekend.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli won the US Grand Prix for Mercedes on Sunday to stand on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion in Mexico next weekend. The 20-year-old Italian did all he could to put the championship out of reach of his rivals in Texas but Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes teammate George Russell did just enough to delay the inevitable with fourth and eighth. Antonelli now needs to score only two points -- a ninth place -- in Mexico to be sure of the title. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished second in Sunday's race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas with Red Bull's Max Verstappen third.

item.title: Voting opens in New Zealand for November 7 election with no clear frontrunner
item.description: Voting opened in New Zealand on Monday for the November 7 general election, with ballot boxes available for nearly two weeks at shopping centres, transport hubs and community halls, ahead of what is expected to be a closely contested race.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Craymer
item.content:encoded: Voting opened in New Zealand on Monday for the November 7 general election, with ballot boxes available for nearly two weeks at shopping centres, transport hubs and community halls, ahead of what is expected to be a closely contested race. The Electoral Commission said 207 voting places were open on Monday, with that number rising to more than 2,300 on election day. Overseas voting [USN:L6N46707J TEXT:"opened"] earlier, on October 21. The race remains [USN:L6N45R12T TEXT:"too close"] to call. Public polling has swung sharply in recent days, underscoring the absence of a clear frontrunner under New Zealand's [USN:L6N43N091 TEXT:"mixed-member proportional"] system, where coalition deals are often needed to form a government. A 1News-Verian poll published on October 20 put the ruling centre-right National Party at 32% and opposition Labour at 27%, while a Post/Freshwater Strategy poll published a day earlier had Labour narrowly ahead on 28.7% to National's 27.6%. In both surveys, the smaller Opportunity party was polling around or above the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament, making it a [USN:L6N44H07U TEXT:"potential kingmaker"]. The start of voting comes just hours after enrolment closed at midnight on Sunday, a deadline that has become one of the campaign's most contentious issues. Unlike in previous elections, voters can no longer enrol or update their details during the voting period, meaning people not enrolled by the cutoff cannot cast a vote in this election. Critics say the earlier cutoff could deter participation, particularly among groups that are harder to reach. The Human Rights Commission said last year that ending election-day enrolment was likely to unjustifiably restrict participation and would disproportionately affect underrepresented groups. As of October 21, 3,729,667 people were enrolled to vote, already above the final 2023 total of 3,688,292, when the enrolment rate was 94.7%, according to the Electoral Commission.

item.title: Proxy advisory firm Glass Lewis backs Bergeron in Ethan Allen fight
item.description: Proxy advisory firm Glass Lewis backed investor Doug Bergeron's campaign to replace all five directors at Ethan Allen , including its octogenarian CEO who has run the iconic U.S. home furnishing company for nearly four decades.
item.dc:creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
item.content:encoded: Proxy advisory firm Glass Lewis backed investor Doug Bergeron's campaign to replace all five directors at Ethan Allen (ETD.N) , including its octogenarian CEO who has run the iconic U.S. home furnishing company for nearly four decades. Doug Bergeron and DGB Investments own 5.2% of the nearly 100-year old company, best known for popularizing colonial wood revival furniture and outfitting the homes of U.S. diplomats, and is pressing to overhaul the company valued at $515 million. Glass Lewis, one of the two leading U.S. firms that guide investor voting on hot-button issues like board elections and corporate merges, threw its weight behind all of the activist investor's director candidates, including Bergeron himself. DGB Investments "appears to have offered investors a credible and reasonably robust strategic and financial agenda alongside an alternate slate more evidently prepared to address muted accountability, operational backsliding and sputtering shareholder value," Glass Lewis wrote in a report seen by Reuters. Investors will vote for directors on November 4. Glass Lewis is the second firm to recommend investors vote for all five of Bergeron's candidates after Egan-Jones Proxy Services last week issued its report. Institutional Investor Services, the biggest and most powerful U.S. proxy firm, has not yet published its report. The campaign at Ethan Allen is one of corporate America's biggest fights as the new proxy season kicks off. Bergeron has argued that he and his director candidates can restore profitable growth and potentially triple shareholder value over three years. Ethan Allen's stock price hast lost more than a quarter of its value over the last 12 months and closed trading at $20.45 on Friday. Bergeron's slate includes executives with experience in the home furnishings businesses, turnarounds, luxury retail and digital strategy. "Ethan Allen is, by most relevant standards, a short-, mid- and long-term underperformer, with incumbent management and the board overseeing near-continuous structural regression and what appears to be an increasingly risky capital program," the Glass Lewis report said. The company has said it will name a successor to CEO Farooq Kathwari, 82, who has led the company for 38 years, no later than June 30, 2027. But Kathwari will lead the company during the search and remain on the board until the 2027 annual meeting. Bergeron called Ethan Allen's proposed succession plan "too little, too late." Ethan Allen did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: US appeals court appears skeptical of Trump DOJ's lawsuit over California voter rolls
item.description: A federal appeals court appeared skeptical on Sunday of a lawsuit filed by President Donald Trump's administration that seeks to force California officials to set aside thousands of mail-in ballots the administration says were sent to noncitizens ahead of midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court appeared skeptical on Sunday of a lawsuit filed by President Donald Trump's administration that seeks to force California officials to set aside thousands of mail-in ballots the administration says were sent to noncitizens ahead of midterm elections. During a rare weekend oral argument, two judges on a three-judge panel of the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals sharply questioned a Justice Department lawyer about the lawsuit, a high-profile effort by the Trump administration to boost the federal government's role in elections ahead of the November 3 midterms. The Department of Justice's lawsuit signals the willingness of Trump's administration to contest midterm results that will decide control of the US Congress, where his fellow Republicans narrowly control both chambers. At the end of the two-hour oral argument, Circuit Judge Mark Bennett said the three-judge panel would try to rule as quickly as possible. Trump's Justice Department has warned election officials across California that they could be targets of federal scrutiny if they refuse to help identify suspected noncitizens on voter rolls. It has distributed to California officials a list of 20,000 people it says are likely aliens registered to vote in the state, a Democratic stronghold. California has said the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust and, in a court filing, stated that the Justice Department's assertions relied on suspect data. All available evidence indicates that ineligible voting, including noncitizen voting, is exceedingly rare. A Reuters investigation this year found just 129 cases in which noncitizens were federally charged with voting illegally; many appeared to stem from voter confusion or administrative errors, rather than intentional fraud. The Justice Department filed its [USN:SPN45000O TEXT:"lawsuit"] on October 15 in federal court in Los Angeles. The lawsuit asked a federal judge to order California to separate any ballots it received from people on the administration's list from the rest of the ballots, and not to count them until it had verified that the people who cast the ballots were citizens. The department filed an emergency motion with the 9th Circuit to expedite the case. Bennett, a Trump-appointed judge, said during Sunday's oral argument that the lawsuit could not be reconciled with a provision of the US Constitution known as the Elections Clause, which gives states the authority to set election processes. "It seems to me that you want us to issue an injunction that is entirely inconsistent with the law that the California legislature has adopted pursuant to the Elections Clause," Bennett told Justice Department attorney Matthew Donnelly. "How can we do that?" The administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the moves as federal overreach. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold, with 52 seats in the House of Representatives — more than any other state. Democrats are seeking to regain control of the House from Trump's fellow Republicans in the midterms. Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through so-called sanctuary state policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. Trump has also long asserted that California's immigration policies have facilitated voter fraud. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, said on Sunday that he was confused by the question of why the appeals court should have jurisdiction to rule at this juncture, noting that the lower court judge assigned to the case had already set a hearing for Tuesday.

item.title: Falcons make key plays, hand 49ers first loss of season
item.description: ATLANTA -- Michael Penix Jr. threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns and rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels had a key fourth-quarter interception on Sunday to help the Atlanta Falcons earn a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ATLANTA -- Michael Penix Jr. threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns and rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels had a key fourth-quarter interception on Sunday to help the Atlanta Falcons earn a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers. Daniels also collected a team-high 11 total tackles and recovered a fumble for Atlanta (3-4), which earned its first home win of the season. Brock Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards and a touchdown, but was picked off twice as San Francisco (6-1) turned over the ball over four times. The Falcons opened the third quarter with a 10-play, 59-yard drive and took a 19-14 lead on Penix's 5-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Pitts Sr. Jessie Bates III intercepted Purdy on the next drive to return the ball to the Falcons at their own 10-yard line. Atlanta then pieced together a 90-yard drive and pushed its lead to 12 on Penix's 21-yard touchdown strike to Drake London on the first play of the fourth. The 49ers reached Atlanta's 23-yard line on the next possession, but Za'Darius Smith's fourth-down sack of Purdy gave the Falcons the ball back with 11:30 remaining. After an Atlanta punt, Purdy hit Kyle Juszczyk for a 1-yard score to cut the deficit to 26-20 with 5:05 left. Eddy Pineiro missed the extra-point attempt. After the Falcons' Jake Bailey shanked a 20-yard punt, Daniels -- who was carted off last week with a neck injury -- intercepted Purdy's pass and returned it to the 49ers' 19 with 2:34 remaining. Nick Folk then knocked through a 31-yarder to make it a two-score game before Bates punched loose a George Kittle fumble, which was recovered by Daniels to seal the win. Christian McCaffrey's 1-yard rushing score on fourth-and-goal gave the visitors a 7-0 lead. Folk's 39-yard field goal made it 7-3. San Francisco took its biggest lead on the first play of the second quarter as Kaelon Black rushed for the first touchdown of his career, a 30-yard scamper to extend the lead to 14-3. Penix answered with a 1-yard touchdown pass to Nick Muse. Folk missed the subsequent extra-point attempt to leave the Falcons' deficit at five. San Francisco fumbled on consecutive plays on its next drive. After 49ers tight end Luke Farrell recovered Jordan James' fumble, Atlanta's Gervon Dexter Sr. recovered Black's miscue at the Falcons' 29-yard line. Folk hit a 33-yarder as time expired to cut Atlanta's halftime deficit to 14-12. --Jack Batten, Field Level Media

item.title: TSE retoma divulgação após prorrogação de horário de votação no 2º turno
item.description: O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) retomou a divulgação dos votos do segundo turno da eleição presidencial deste domingo após decisão do ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), de prorrogar em duas horas o horário de votação, até as 19h.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões, Maria Marcello, Victor Borges
item.content:encoded: O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) retomou a divulgação dos votos do segundo turno da eleição presidencial deste domingo após decisão do ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), de prorrogar em duas horas o horário de votação, até as 19h. Com 0,37% das seções eleitorais apuradas logo após a retomada, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) liderava com 55,53% dos votos válidos, enquanto o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) somava 44,47%, mostraram dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). A prorrogação do horário de votação em duas horas abrangeu apenas as urnas que ainda estavam abertas, segundo Zanin, mas levou o TSE a suspender temporariamente a totalização dos votos "Sem prejuízo das apurações necessárias oportunamente e suas consequências jurídicas, determino que a decisão seja cumprida nos locais onde as urnas não foram fechadas, com a posterior totalização dos votos nas condições enunciadas, sendo que, nas urnas que já foram fechadas os votos serão computados e totalizados, nos termos anteriormente mencionados", disse Zanin. Apesar das decisões, diante da ausência de comunicação oficial por um bom tempo, muitas das seções fecharam normalmente às 17h, impedindo a retomada da votação nesses locais. Mesários de diferentes capitais brasileiras relataram que as seções eleitorais foram encerradas no horário original. "Deu 17h02, no máximo, pediram para encerrar. Nós encerramos as urnas e fomos embora", disse Renata Araújo, mesária em uma escola na zona norte de São Paulo. No Rio de Janeiro, por volta das 17h40, mesários continuavam em uma escola que serviu como local de votação, mas as seções já tinham sido encerradas. Segundo uma testemunha ouvida pela Reuters, eles foram orientados a não publicar os boletins de urna até as 19h. Um mesário de uma escola em Porto Alegre disse que nenhuma informação sobre a decisão de prorrogar a votação havia chegado à seção até as 17h, quando as urnas foram fechadas no local. Ele relatou ter recebido uma mensagem do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Estado (TRE-RS) às 17h22min. "Não recebemos comunicação oficial alguma até 17h21. Podem levar as mídias até o presidente de local e os presidentes de local levar mídias até o ponto designado", diz a mensagem. A Reuters questionou o TRE-RS sobre o conteúdo, mas ainda não teve retorno. CRONOGRAMA O adiamento do horário de encerramento da votação teve como origem pedido da campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) alegando falta de ônibus nas cidades de Salvador, Feira de Santana e Lauro de Freitas, todas na Bahia. Posteriormente, a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) também pediu a ampliação da votação por mais duas horas em cidades de São Paulo, Paraná e Santa Catarina devido às condições climáticas nessas regiões. Diante dos pedidos das campanhas e de relatos nas redes sociais de dificuldades de transporte de eleitores, Zanin decidiu pela prorrogação. Apesar da prorrogação, o TSE divulgou uma primeira parcial de resultados mostrando que, com 0,25% das seções eleitorais apuradas, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) tinha 57,66% dos votos válidos contra 42,34% do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Minutos depois da divulgação da primeira parcial dos resultados da disputa presidencial, o TSE anunciou a suspensão da totalização dos votos do segundo turno da eleição.

item.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to student led movement in parliamentary election
item.description: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in parliamentary elections on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Donovan
item.content:encoded: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to the student-led protest movement in parliamentary elections on Sunday. "We still do not have final results, on the basis of a sample ... it is clear that we have lost these elections, the Student List has won, they will have between 135 and 140 seats and we will have 105, no one else has entered parliament," Vucic said. The snap elections, called by Vucic in September, came after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. The students have since gained widespread support to become the greatest threat to Vucic since he first became prime minister in 2014 and then president in 2017.

item.title: Giants beat Texans in OT on Devin Singletary's walkoff TD
item.description: Devin Singletary ran for a 30-yard touchdown in overtime to defeat his former team and propel the visiting New York Giants to a 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Devin Singletary ran for a 30-yard touchdown in overtime to defeat his former team and propel the visiting New York Giants to a 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon. The Giants (4-2-1) forced the Texans (2-5) to punt on the first overtime possession, which meant the next score would win. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy flipped a quick completion to Malik Nabers in the left flat for nine yards and Skattebo zipped 42 yards to the Houston 30. On the next snap, with the Giants looking to center the ball for the potential game-winning field goal, McCarthy handed the ball to Singletary on a draw and he broke through the left side for the touchdown. McCarthy won his debut start with the Giants and his fifth consecutive start overall. The early-season acquisition from the Minnesota Vikings completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. Skattebo had 17 carries for 124 yards, Singletary ran five times for 41 yards and Nabers caught seven passes for 111 yards for the Giants. C.J. Stroud completed 17 of 28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans, who dropped to 0-4 at home. Woody Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and tight end Dalton Schultz had five catches for 45 yards. After the Texans sacked McCarthy for the third time to force a punt, Houston marched for a touchdown in the final minute to make the Giants go to overtime for the second time in three weeks. Not long after limping to the medical tent with what appeared to be a significant left leg injury, Marks carried Houston down the field to set up the game-tying score. He had a 15-yard catch and 7-yard run to move the Texans to the Giants' 15 at the two-minute warning. The Texans ran wide receiver Xavier Hutchinson on consecutive plays in the red zone. Then, on third-and-goal at the Giants' 3, C.J. Stroud sprinted out to his right and hit Hutchinson for a touchdown to tie it at 21 with 52 seconds remaining. Former Giants starting quarterback Jameis Winston made multiple integral cameo appearances, primarily in short-yardage situations. He plunged for the 1-yard run in the third that boosted to New York's lead to 14-6 and also converted multiple critical first downs. With the game 14-14 and the Giants facing fourth-and-1 at the Houston 33, Winston blasted ahead for two yards on the 10th play of the 14-play, 80-yard drive New York used to take the lead. Cam Skattebo rumbled 16 yards to score with 8:55 left. He broke a tackle at the 13, spun into more contact at the 10 but broke another tackle, then used his left arm to shove Texans safety Calen Bullock backward twice as he crossed the goal line. Stroud connected with Marvin Harrison Jr. on a rapid release laser to the center of the end zone to tie it up at 14 with 34 seconds left in the first half. Harrison Jr. aligned in the right slot and settled quickly in the middle of the field for the 6-yard score, his only reception of the game. Houston was on its heels in the first half dealing with a hyper-aggressive game plan from the Giants. The Texans managed only a pair of field goals from Ka'imi Fairbairn -- 58 yards in the first quarter and 57 in the second -- before the Harrison score. McCarthy completed six of his first seven passes for 106 yards, featuring a 42-yard deep ball to Nabers down the right sideline to set up Tyrone Tracy's third touchdown of the season. He powered in from two yards out and the Giants jumped ahead 7-3. Tracy left the game with a hamstring injury with 5:20 remaining in the second quarter. He grabbed the back of his left leg after gaining a first down and limped to the sideline. Tracy had six carries for 15 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: Zelenskiy says US warnings on ballistic strikes have fully resumed
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said US warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes, critical to Ukraine's air defences, had been fully restored after recent issues.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said US warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes, critical to Ukraine's air defences, had been fully restored after recent issues. Speaking to Ukraine's TSN television channel, he said SpaceX's (SPCX.O) Starshield satellite internet had been working at speeds of up to 420 kilometres per hour since early on Saturday morning, after it had been throttled earlier in October amid diplomatic pressure on Kyiv from Washington. Zelenskiy said he discussed both issues in a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, casting the changes as results of that meeting. Speaking about the upcoming technical talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington in November, Zelenskiy said Ukraine would not discuss limits to its armed forces, or enforced post-war neutrality. Kyiv has long sought entry into the NATO alliance despite the reticence of some members. Zelenskiy also renewed his push for a trilateral US-brokered meeting between him and Vladimir Putin. The Ukrainian leader has long argued Putin is the only person in Russia who can make major decisions to end the war or meaningfully discuss core issues, such as the fate of the nearly 20% of Ukraine that Russia occupies. "The issue of territories is a red line that can be discussed exclusively at the level of leaders," Zelenskiy said.

item.title: Browns defeat Titans with third walkoff FG this season
item.description: Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of Sunday afternoon's 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville, Tenn.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of Sunday afternoon's 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville, Tenn. After Tennessee tied it 24-24 with 58 seconds remaining on Tony Pollard's third touchdown of the day, Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards with 28 seconds left. Szmyt, who missed from 43 yards in the fourth quarter, booted the winner to keep the Browns (5-2) atop the AFC North. Watson eclipsed 300 yards for the first time with the Browns as he completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and an interception. He also rushed for a score. Quinshon Judkins carried 17 times for 96 yards with two scores. KC Concepcion had eight receptions for 129 yards. The Titans (1-6) came in off a 26-20 road win over Indianapolis and saw Cam Ward go 20-for-31 for 181 yards and an interception. Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards. The Titans scored on their opening series for the first time this season as Pollard carried five times for 60 yards, which included 36 yards for a score. Cor'Dale Flott's 14-yard interception return set up the Titans again. Pollard capitalized on a toss sweep from 10 yards out to double the advantage at 8:35, the second rushing score against a Browns defense that had surrendered just one in 2026. Judkins had a 5-yard touchdown run with 5:32 left in the first quarter. Cleveland kept it a one-score game by stuffing Pollard on fourth down at the 1 with 9:34 left in the half. The teams exchanged turnovers as Cleveland's Denzel Ward picked off Cam Ward after a Browns fumble, which set up Judkins' second rushing score from 6 yards out at 2:17. Szmyt's 28-yard field goal on the half's final play put the Browns up 17-14. The visitors were unable to add on in the first minute of the fourth after Szmyt's errant 43-yard attempt. However, the Titans' Joey Slye evened it at 17 with a 29-yard kick with 8:41 left. The Browns engineered a 71-yard drive, highlighted by Dylan Sampson's 19-yard run and Concepcion's 18-yard reception that set up Watson's keeper from 9 yards out for the 24-17 lead with 4:34 left. Ward answered by leading the Titans on a 63-yard march capped by Pollard's 1-yard plunge with 58 seconds left for the tie. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bengals use big second-half rally to roll past Ravens
item.description: Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and the Cincinnati Bengals scored 35 unanswered points to record a 35-13 victory over the host Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and the Cincinnati Bengals scored 35 unanswered points to record a 35-13 victory over the host Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Burrow completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards while leading five touchdown drives in the half as Cincinnati (4-2) overcame a 13-0 halftime deficit to stun the Ravens (4-3). Overall, he was 22-for-30 passing for 292 yards. Tee Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase, Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample also caught touchdown passes and Samaje Perine rushed for a score for the Bengals. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson (ankle) missed his third straight game for the Ravens. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley again drew the start and completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 298 yards. He threw one touchdown and one interception. Zay Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards and one score for Baltimore, which blew a double-digit lead for the second straight week. The Ravens have been outscored 48-0 over their last two second halves. The Cleveland Browns outscored them 13-0 last Sunday after the Ravens went up 10-0 at the half. Cincinnati got on the board with 9:24 remaining in the third quarter as Burrow's 6-yard scoring throw to Gesicki capped a nine-play, 66-yard drive. The Bengals took the lead less than five minutes later when Burrow connected on a 13-yard touchdown pass to Higgins with 4:29 to play in the period. Baltimore passed on a potential go-ahead field goal at the start of the fourth quarter. The Ravens instead went for it on fourth-and-2 from the Cincinnati 12, but Huntley's pass to tight end Josh Cuevas was incomplete. The Bengals answered by driving 88 yards in six plays. Burrow hit Higgins for 44 yards and Perine later scored on a 1-yard run to give Cincinnati a 21-13 lead with 11:14 left in regulation. The Bengals continued their comeback on the next drive as Burrow hit Chase for 30 yards and Higgins for 43 on back-to-back plays to move to the Baltimore 6. Three plays later, Burrow hit Chase for a 2-yard scoring pass to make it a 15-point margin, 28-13. On Baltimore's next play, Huntley's pass was deflected and Cincinnati's Demetrius Knight corralled the ball for an interception. Knight returned it 14 yards to the Ravens 24-yard line. Three plays later, Burrow tossed a 16-yard scoring pass to Sample to make it 35-13 with 6:21 left. Baltimore started fast, scoring on its fourth play from scrimmage. Huntley threw to his right to Flowers at the line of scrimmage, and Flowers broke free for a 48-yard catch-and-run touchdown. The Ravens tacked on two Tyler Loop field goals in the second quarter after long possessions that stalled. A drive of 78 yards on 18 plays that lasted 11 minutes ended with a 34-yard field goal, and a 13-play, 82-yard drive that lasted 6:09 led to a 24-yarder with 50 seconds left. Cincinnati possessed the ball for just 7:40 in the first half while being outgained 258-59. --Field Level Media

item.title: Supremo Tribunal Federal de Brasil amplía en dos horas horario de votación en balotaje presidencial
item.description: El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal de Brasil Cristiano Zanin ordenó el domingo que se ampliara en dos horas el horario de votación de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal de Brasil Cristiano Zanin ordenó el domingo que se ampliara en dos horas el horario de votación de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. En un principio, estaba previsto que las urnas cerraran a las 17:00 hora de Brasilia (2000 GMT). La campaña de Lula denunció que las autoridades de varias ciudades estaban restringiendo el acceso de los votantes al transporte público. En tanto, la autoridad electoral del país anunció que suspendía el recuento de los sufragios hasta que se cumpla el horario ampliado de la votación.

item.title: Terland strikes late to give Man United derby draw with City in WSL
item.description: Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser to knock visitors Manchester City off top spot in the Women's Super League table on Sunday evening as a hotly contested derby finished 1-1 at the Leigh Sports Ground.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser to knock visitors Manchester City off top spot in the Women's Super League table on Sunday evening as a hotly contested derby finished 1-1 at the Leigh Sports Ground. Reigning champions City dropped points for the first time this season, allowing Chelsea to go top on goal difference after they came back from a goal down to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 earlier in the day. Chelsea and City both have 19 points, with London City Lionesses third on 16 and Manchester United fourth on 11. Making her 100th WSL appearance, Bunny Shaw gave City the lead in the 66th minute, brushing off the challenge of Dominique Janssen and rattling a shot into the far corner to break the deadlock and silence the home fans, who booed and heckled her throughout. The game looked to be getting away from United until a well-worked freekick was lofted into the box in the 89th minute, and Norway international Terland was on hand to blast the ball into the net to grab a point for her side. On Merseyside, Liverpool's Jana Fernandez Velasco struck deep into stoppage time to snatch a 2-2 draw at home to London City. Aston Villa raced out to a 3-0 lead over Everton by the 50th minute with Amalie Vangsgaard scoring twice, but the home side scored twice late on to ensure a nervous finish as Villa held on for a 3-2 win. Charlton Athletic's miserable run continued as they slumped to their seventh straight defeat. Substitute Wilma Leidhammar scored the only goal of the game for Birmingham City in the 68th minute to leave Charlton still firmly rooted to the bottom of the table and searching for their first point of the season.

item.title: Shadab heroics lift Pakistan past England in one-wicket thriller
item.description: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as the hosts rallied from 154-9 to secure a one-wicket win over England in Lahore on Sunday and book their place in the tri-series final.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as the hosts rallied from 154-9 to secure a one-wicket win over England in Lahore on Sunday and book their place in the tri-series final. Chasing 242 for victory, Pakistan appeared to be heading towards defeat after England's bowlers reduced them to 154-9 in the 34th over. However, Shadab launched a superb counter-attack and, with Rauf making an unbeaten seven off 19 balls, guided the hosts to victory with 17 balls to spare. Their 89-run partnership was the highest for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase. Earlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs despite Ben Duckett's composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling effort with 4-46 to dismantle England's top order. The defeat was England's third successive loss in the tri-series after Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, reaching a target of 430 with one ball to spare. Afridi struck in the opening over to dismiss Tom Banton before removing Joe Root in the third over, while Jordan Cox fell to Haris Rauf as England slumped to 52-4. Ben Duckett and Sam Curran steadied the innings with a fifth-wicket partnership of 93. Curran made 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped take England past 200, while Gus Atkinson finished unbeaten on 36. Pakistan lost Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam for 10 apiece before Saad Baig struck a brisk 32 off 22 balls and Salman Ali Agha made 26 to briefly revive the chase. Shadab Khan came to the crease in the 24th over with the hosts struggling at 103-6. Shadab, who struck 13 fours and five sixes, was given out lbw to Atkinson with 21 runs needed, but successfully reviewed the decision after replays showed an inside edge.

item.title: Malik Willis guides Dolphins past Jets for long-sought first win
item.description: Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help the Miami Dolphins pick up their first win, beating the New York Jets 28-25 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help the Miami Dolphins pick up their first win, beating the New York Jets 28-25 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards without an interception and rushed for 37 yards on eight attempts to help give head coach Jeff Hafley his first NFL victory. Willis' final run -- not counting two kneel-downs that followed -- was a 2-yard quarterback sneak on fourth-and-1 from the Jets' 49, which sealed the outcome as Miami converted with less than two minutes left and New York was out of timeouts. Ollie Gordon II ran for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries as Miami (1-5) rushed for 156 yards overall. The ground game helped seal the result on its final drive of the fourth quarter. The Jets (2-5) lost for the fifth time in six games and lost their eighth consecutive game against an AFC East opponent. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception to lead the Jets. Smith's third touchdown pass was a 12-yarder to Mason Taylor, who caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns. Smith connected with Taylor on a two-point conversion to cut the Dolphins' lead to three with 3:24 left. But the Dolphins ran out the clock by converting a pair of first downs, beginning with a 14-yard run by Gordon. Braelon Allen started again for injured running back Breece Hall and ran for 104 yards on 17 carries, also catching six passes for 30 yards. Omar Cooper Jr. caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown. The Dolphins scored touchdowns on their first two drives for the first time this season, and led a game for the first time all year following Willis' 7-yard touchdown pass to Douglas, who returned to action Sunday after missing Miami's prior three games with an ankle injury. The lead lasted 2:16 until the Jets answered with a 13-yard touchdown pass from Smith to Taylor. But the Dolphins responded with a 14-play, 60-yard drive capped by a 1-yard dive up the middle by Gordon to take a 14-7 lead. The Dolphins took a 28-17 edge with 4:55 left in the fourth when Willis found Douglas down the sideline for a 63-yard score, giving Miami its highest scoring output of the season. --Field Level Media
